content.comment_body: Earlier, I asked about an AC current sensor for monitoring exported current from a micro hydro setup using [product_name] analogue input. The 0-10v DC output LEM sensors were suggested and I've ordered an AT 50 B10. Thank you! I also know someone with a similar micro-hydro setup who needs the same sensor, but their [product_name] is located 300 meters from the grid connection, with no direct wiring possible unless digging up the field. However, there is fibre-based ethernet available between both points. Is the LEM sensor with 0-10v DC output still suitable for this? After researching wireless transmission options, I found devices online, but the costs are very high. [url] Does anyone know of more budget-friendly ethernet or wireless solutions? Thanks in advance.

Hello, If dedicated wireless solutions are too expensive, you could place a second [product_name] unit at the sensor location and transmit sensor data between the two [product_name] devices. Hope this is useful.

analysis.insight_summary: Forum participants are searching for an economical way to transmit analog sensor data across a 300-meter gap, where direct cabling would be impractical. They wish to use the available Ethernet connection to link sensors with a [product_name] module. High costs for specialized wireless transmitters have been cited as a major issue.
analysis.user_expectations: Users are looking for a cost-effective and straightforward method to send analog sensor data over long distances (around 300 meters), ideally making use of Ethernet or standard wireless communication, without relying on expensive wireless hardware.
